statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-70354 (GHSA-gg8c-3338-xw2f) is an out-of-bounds write in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that allows local code execution. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (win-*) as the only affected .NET 9 package, fixed in 9.0.19 (https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/security/advisories/GHSA-gg8c-3338-xw2f, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/432, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.19/9.0.19.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: none of them contains the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App runtime or any WPF or Windows Forms assembly (PresentationCore, PresentationFramework, System.Xaml, System.Windows.Forms and the like), and none contains a native Windows PE file. WPF names appear only as IntelliSense XML documentation files in Microsoft.Private.Intellisense reference packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, a Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport package in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts holds runtime libraries such as System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Diagnostics.EventLog and no WPF or Windows Forms assembly, and WindowsBase.dll appears only as the .NET compatibility facade in the .NET shared framework and its runtime, ILCompiler and reference packs, not the WPF implementation.
